projects.title: Dual-Write Migration Lab with Built-In Sabotage
projects.pitch: Build a small orders service, then migrate it live from a legacy Postgres schema to a new store while a load generator keeps writing. The service has a phase-aware router covering dual-write, backfill, verify, and cutover. Add a chaos switch that reproduces each failure mode from the article: backfilling before dual-write, a stale backfill overwriting fresh writes, and shadow-write failures taking down the primary. Then prove your design survives each one.
stack: SQLite or DuckDB as target store
k6 or Locust for write load
you_will_learn: Consistency during dual-write windows and why write ordering matters
Keyset-cursor backfill versus OFFSET pagination
Last-writer-wins with version columns to stop stale backfill overwrites
Decoupling shadow-write availability using async queues and failure budgets
Continuous sampling verification and row-conservation accounting at stage boundaries
milestones: Build the CRUD service plus a load generator writing about 200 rows/sec
Implement the phase-aware router with feature-flag phases
Write a keyset backfill with deterministic natural keys and idempotent upserts
Add a sampling verifier that reports mismatch rate and fails loudly on a count-ratio floor
Add a chaos mode that injects each of the four failure modes and shows the verifier catches them
Do cutover and rollback with zero dropped writes, proven by end-to-end row counts

projects.title: Freshness-Budgeted Online Feature Store
projects.pitch: Model an online feature store as a materialized view over an event stream. Clickstream events flow through Redpanda/Kafka into a recompute worker that writes features to Redis, with Postgres as the source of truth. Each feature declares a freshness budget, and the serving API returns the value together with its measured staleness. It also refuses or falls back when it can tell the budget is unachievable under the current stream lag.
you_will_learn: Treating staleness as a first-class SLO and measuring it correctly
How consumer lag propagates into serving freshness
Why phase-locked request and recompute clocks under-observe staleness, and how jittered sampling fixes it
Cache invalidation versus recompute-on-write trade-offs
Graceful degradation with fallback values and budget-violation signals
milestones: Build an event producer and a consumer that recomputes rolling-window features into Redis with event-time stamps
Add a serving endpoint that returns feature, age, and in-budget flag
Add Prometheus histograms for staleness and consumer lag
Reproduce the phase-locking measurement bias, then fix it with randomized probe timing
Derive the minimum achievable staleness per feature from the paper's threshold idea and reject infeasible budgets at registration
Inject lag spikes by pausing consumers and verify alerts and fallbacks

projects.title: Resilience Harness for a Tool-Using Agent Pipeline
projects.pitch: Take a small RAG plus tool-calling agent (for example, one that answers questions using MCP tools) and wrap every component in production resilience patterns from the 150-incident taxonomy. These include circuit breakers on tools, output quality gates on generation, bulkheads between retrieval and tool calls, and timeouts with budgets. Then build a fault-injection runner that measures how much each pattern actually reduces bad answers and outages.
stack: An MCP server (via openai/mcp-extensions-style plugin or the reference SDK)
A local open-weight model or hosted API
you_will_learn: Circuit breaker state machines (closed, open, half-open) applied to flaky tools
Output quality gates as schema validation and grounding checks
Component isolation and bulkheads to stop cascading failures
Designing fault-injection experiments with baselines and measurable outcomes
Distributed tracing across LLM, retrieval, and tool spans
milestones: Build a baseline agent with a vector-store retriever and 2–3 MCP tools, with end-to-end OTel traces
Write a fault injector that adds tool latency, 5xx errors, empty retrieval, malformed JSON output, and context overflow
Add a circuit breaker and timeout budget per tool
Add an output quality gate with retry or abstain policy
Build a bulkhead executor to isolate retrieval from tool concurrency
Produce a report table of failure mode by pattern, showing success-rate deltas over 500 injected runs

projects.title: Precedence Forest Log Triage Engine
projects.pitch: Build a LOGOS-style unsupervised triage tool. It ingests raw logs from a deliberately broken microservice demo and extracts entities (hosts, request IDs, services) and event templates. It computes co-occurrence and temporal precedence, then compresses an alert flood into a small forest showing how the failure propagated. A final optional step feeds the forest to an LLM for a root-cause summary.
stack: A 3–4 service demo app run under Podman compose
you_will_learn: Streaming log parsing and template extraction
Indexing events by entity and time window for fast co-occurrence queries
Inferring temporal precedence and handling clock skew across hosts
Noise reduction and alert deduplication as a compression problem
Observability pipeline design for backpressure in the collector
milestones: Build the demo services plus a fault script (DB pool exhaustion cascading to upstream timeouts)
Write an ingestor with template mining and entity extraction, storing events in DuckDB
Compute a co-occurrence matrix and precedence edges over sliding windows
Prune to a precedence forest and render it as a DOT or HTML graph
Measure noise reduction ratio and alert consolidation factor on 3 injected incidents
Optionally feed the forest to an LLM and compare root-cause accuracy against raw logs

projects.title: Backpressure-Aware Gateway for a Local MoE Inference Engine
projects.pitch: Put a scheduling gateway in front of a local LLM engine such as DwarfStar 4 or llama.cpp that serves several clients at once. It covers admission control, separate prefill and decode queues, token-based rate limits, request deadlines, and load shedding. The goal is to keep p99 time-to-first-token bounded when the single box is overloaded, applying the latency-critical versus best-effort split from GPU-sharing research on a laptop.
stack: vegeta or a custom load generator
you_will_learn: Backpressure, bounded queues, and why unbounded queues destroy tail latency
Admission control and load shedding with deadline-aware rejection
Priority scheduling of interactive versus batch requests
Separating prefill and decode costs when modeling capacity
Measuring TTFT, tokens/sec, and p99 under open-loop load
milestones: Build a streaming proxy to the local engine with per-request TTFT and throughput metrics
Run an open-loop load test that shows latency collapse with a naive FIFO
Add a bounded queue with token-cost estimates and 429 or Retry-After shedding
Add two priority classes, with interactive preempting batch at queue level
Add per-request deadlines that drop work which can't finish in time
Write up before/after p99 TTFT and goodput curves
